name: The Cairn of the Last Crown
history: During the final years of the Lost Holds, a small procession carried a royal burial to an isolated shrine rather than interring the deceased within the ancestral strongholds. The surviving entrance was sealed and concealed beneath the shrine’s stone platform. Generations of Blackpick families have preserved conflicting accounts of the burial.
current_state: The shrine is partially buried by rockfall. Its outer platform remains accessible, but the burial chambers have not knowingly been entered in living memory. Recent erosion has exposed a fragment of carved stone beneath the platform.
inhabitants: Mountain wildlife around the shrine. The presence of guardians, undead, or other occupants within the tomb is undetermined.
danger_level: Low at the shrine; potentially moderate to high within the sealed tomb, depending on its surviving protections.
discovery: A sheltered mountainside beneath an old dwarven shrine. Borin Blackpick knows competing versions of the family legend. Comparing oral accounts with surviving funerary carvings or old route descriptions may identify the shrine.
site_type: tomb | Ancient sites | Ancient dwarven burial chamber; mountain shrine
points_of_interest:
Weathered shrine; carved lintel fragment; stone platform; concealed burial entrance; funerary inscriptions; royal burial chamber; possible records of the last years of the Lost Holds.

Unresolved elements: Identity of the interred ruler; contents and condition of the burial; truth of the warning concerning stolen possessions and the third sunrise; whether any descendants recognize a duty of guardianship.
